findings.title: Expected sold-out / idempotency 409s are graded as k6 traffic failures, so the flagship surge always finalizes failed
findings.summary: The generated k6 script never overrides response classification, so k6's built-in http_req_failed counts the buy path's expected 409s (sold_out, idempotency_conflict) as failures. Surge presets that oversubscribe stock therefore report ~0.9 failure rate and finalize failed with traffic_delivery_major_shortfall despite perfect delivery. The path is untested and one grading test encodes the wrong behavior as correct.

findings.title: Run-scoped ERP behavior and worker backpressure are frozen into the run but never applied
findings.summary: Preset erp and backpressure blocks are frozen into demo_runs.config_snapshot but nothing applies them at run time: the Mock ERP always decides from its global chaos store and the worker's BullMQ concurrency is fixed from env. surge-10k, advertised as a slow and failing ERP, runs against a fast always-succeeding one; workerConcurrency and public-custom ERP knobs are inert.

findings.title: Root pnpm test:db:migrate is a stale "not implemented" placeholder that errors out
findings.summary: The root script still runs the Task-1.3-era not-implemented guard and exits 1, while the real implementation exists in packages/db and three docs walk the reader through the root command as a working migration-authoring aid.

findings.title: Catalog (null-runId) buy against a live run's generated offer leaks a Redis hold
findings.summary: The run sale-eligibility pre-gate only runs when runId is set. A buy with no runId against a run-owned offer decrements Redis stock, is rejected by the run-ownership trigger at persistence, and the ApiError is re-thrown without releasing the hold — a repeatable public stock drain that produces no durable order.

findings.title: demo_run_reservation_outcomes is a dead durable table despite comments claiming active use
findings.summary: The table, its enum, and its constraints are never written or read anywhere, yet multiple comments assert it is the Phase 10 durable outcome record. The sold-out accounting it was meant to hold actually lands in demo_run_summaries.terminalInventorySnapshot.

findings.title: orders:process completed jobs are never trimmed, so the completed set grows unbounded during the surge
findings.summary: defaultJobOptions omit removeOnComplete (unlike the notification queue), so a surge-10k run leaves ~10k completed job hashes in Redis, accumulating across runs until an explicit admin obliterate.

findings.title: Traffic metrics are forwarded only once, after k6 exits, so there is no live in-run traffic telemetry
findings.summary: The orchestrator reads the k6 JSON output only after the process exits and forwards the whole batch in one POST, so live traffic panels have nothing to render during the run and jump to final values at completion — worst for long soak runs.

findings.title: Live dashboard retains the previous run's order-outcome overlay across a run change
findings.summary: The recovery reducer re-baselines the snapshot but deliberately keeps the live overlay with no run-change detection. A run that emits no order events (notably a clean sold-out-only run) shows the previous run's confirmed/failed counts and lastOrderEvent as current for its entire duration.

findings.title: API readiness never probes Redis reachability; a down Redis is hidden as degraded/HTTP 200
findings.summary: Redis is only checked for configuration presence while PostgreSQL gets a real probe. With Redis down — the inventory hot-path authority — every buy returns 503 while /health/ready, the compose healthcheck, health:check, and runtime:smoke all stay green.

findings.title: WEB_ORIGIN is documented and compose-injected as the API realtime-CORS allow-list, but no code implements CORS
findings.summary: WEB_ORIGIN is read nowhere and no CORS plugin is registered. The demo works same-origin through the proxy, but an operator exposing the debug ports and relying on WEB_ORIGIN gets no protection — a false security claim in docs and compose.

findings.title: Concurrent idempotent replay can return reservation_secured for an order that will never exist
findings.summary: A replayed duplicate decides secured-vs-pending from a pending sentinel the original request only writes after its durable write has already failed. Under a concurrent same-key duplicate plus a transient write failure, the replay promises a queued order that reconciliation will never materialize.

findings.title: PUBLIC_CUSTOM_* env knobs are inert; the public runtime policy is hardcoded in the seed
findings.summary: Thirteen documented PUBLIC_CUSTOM_* variables are read by no code — the policy is DEFAULT_PUBLIC_RUNTIME_POLICY seeded verbatim, and one variable (MAX_ERP_MAX_TPS) has no representable policy field at all.

findings.title: Live inventory.updated publish is awaited inline on the winning hot path
findings.summary: A best-effort observability publish is awaited before the durable write on every newly reserved buy, adding a serialized Redis round trip to the latency-critical winning path for no correctness benefit.

findings.title: clearRunLiveState leaks the run's sale-eligibility Redis key on cleanup
findings.summary: The cleanup helper unlinks outcome, metrics, and inventory keys but not run:{runId}:sale-eligibility, which lingers until its 24h TTL — and the smoke by-id path destroys a run whose eligibility record still says accepting.

findings.title: resetTestDatabase performs DROP SCHEMA / TRUNCATE with no guard that the target is actually a test database
findings.summary: Safety rests entirely on callers passing TEST_DATABASE_URL; a future caller or a mis-set env var pointing at the dev database would silently wipe development data.

findings.title: Seed is idempotent for durable rows but hard-resets Redis inventory
findings.summary: Re-running the seed leaves durable rows untouched but unconditionally resets the catalog offer's live Redis counters to full stock, diverging from any existing reservations against that offer.

findings.title: Worker readiness reports order_process_worker_running: ok even when the consumer is not consuming
findings.summary: BullMQ's Worker.isRunning() does not reflect broker connectivity; with Redis unreachable the worker retries forever, consumes nothing, and /health/ready still reports the loop healthy while orders pile up.

findings.title: A confirmation persisted-transition failure can double-confirm at the (non-idempotent) Mock ERP
findings.summary: The ERP confirm precedes markConfirmed; a crash or transient failure between them redelivers the job and confirms at the ERP again, since the Mock ERP has no per-orderId dedup despite the request carrying a stable orderId.

findings.title: Admin console cannot launch the admin-only / Custom presets it can create
findings.summary: The admin console reuses the public RunControls with its four hard-coded public presets, so there is no UI to start the admin-only or Custom presets the management panel can create — the backend supports it; the launcher is missing.

findings.title: formatClock slices the ISO string as if it were always UTC
findings.summary: The clock renders iso.slice(11, 19), but the shared schema permits explicit offsets; a non-Z producer would render offset-local wall-clock time mislabeled as UTC. Latent because producers currently emit Z.

findings.title: DB run-summary/finalization tables carry summary columns that are never written, read, or in the contract
findings.summary: Several jsonb columns on demo_run_summaries and demo_run_finalizations exist only in the schema and initial migration — dead schema and DB-to-contract drift signaling an abandoned richer-summary feature.

findings.title: requestFailureRate is documented as (0..1) but only bounded below
findings.summary: Both schema fields use z.number().min(0) with no .max(1), unlike the comparable ERP rate fields; a malformed over-range producer value would silently validate.

findings.title: Unused contract exports add vocabulary surface with no consumer
findings.summary: SIMULATED_PURCHASE_STATUSES and trafficSnapshotRefSchema are exported but consumed nowhere; the UI derives its purchase view from other schemas, leaving it ambiguous whether these were supposed to be used.

findings.title: runtime:smoke:load permanently lowers the admin-soak-steady preset and never restores it
findings.summary: The smoke shrinks the editable preset to run quickly but has no restore step, contradicting its own clean-up-only-what-it-created contract; the seeded 2-minute soak silently becomes a 5-second run.

findings.title: The only real-k6 end-to-end test self-skips silently; the k6 parsers are otherwise validated solely against hand-authored canned JSON
findings.summary: describe.skipIf(!k6Available) means any environment without k6 on PATH reports green with zero coverage of the real k6-format-to-parser contract; every other k6 test uses canned JSON written to match the parser.

findings.title: ERP timeout vs admin latency cap mismatch
findings.summary: The worker's 2000ms ERP request timeout sits below the Mock ERP's 5000ms admin latency cap, so global chaos latency in (2000, 5000]ms turns "slow ERP" into universal timeouts rather than slow-but-successful confirmations.

findings.title: run:catalog:order-outcomes aggregate is never cleared
findings.summary: Catalog (null-runId) traffic increments the CATALOG_RUN_SCOPE order-outcome hash, which carries no TTL and is not covered by run cleanup — harmless but ever-growing.

findings.title: Rate-named metrics store per-request counter deltas, not rates
findings.summary: k6 JSON points carry per-observation values (http_reqs = 1 per request), and the latest-point projection keeps only the last one, so the stored "request rate" ends up 1 and "failure rate" the last request's 0/1.

findings.title: markTrafficFailed sets finalizedAt = trafficEndedAt
findings.summary: Defensible, but it is the one path where trafficEndedAt and finalizedAt are the same instant; worth confirming history consumers never infer state from timestamp equality.
